newsitem.title: CHINA: China primary industry investment up 151.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: China primary industry investment up 151.5 pct.

text.p: China's investment in its primary industry, which includes farming, forestry, animal husbandry, fishery and water conservancy, hit 1.3 billion yuan in the first two months of the year, up 151.5 percent from the same period in 1995, official figures showed on Thursday.
Investment in second industry, including industry and construction, in January-February was 22.95 billion yuan, up 12.2 percent, the State Statistical Bureau figures showed.
Investment in tertiary industry, or services, reached 34.6 billion yuan, up 19.9 percent year-on-year, it said.
In a more detailed breakdown, the bureau said China invested 22.7 billion yuan in industry in the first two months of this year, up 12.6 percent from the same period of 1996.
In January-February, China poured 11.1 billion yuan into fixed assets of the energy sector, representing a 21.5 percent increase, it said.
The raw materials sector, including metallurgy, non-ferrous metals, chemicals and forestry, received a combined investment of 4.71 billion yuan, down 13.5 percent, it said.
Investment in the machinery and electronics sector was 1.75 billion yuan, down 23.8 percent from a year ago, it said.
Investment in light industry and the textile industry jumped to 3.44 billion yuan, up 80.3 percent, it said.
